speaker: client
text:
Hi Marissa,

Before we settle the job arrangement, I wanted to see how the brand work is progressing. You acknowledged the invitation I sent for the landing-page job, but I did not receive a further proposal, which is fine. Since we have already discussed the website, should I simply send you an offer? If so, would you propose an hourly or fixed-price engagement? We would then need to agree either a rate and time estimate or a price, depending on the model.

Two job-related issues are priorities:

1\. To confirm "used in business," I urgently need some form of landing page with a sign-up button. That will allow me to submit a trademark application and obtain a DUNS number.

2\. As I work on the UI/UX implementation, we need to confirm the layout and style of the UI shell. I have attached screenshots of a quick PoC built with the target development stack to illustrate what I have in mind.

Thanks,
Derek

speaker: freelancer
text:
Hi Derek,

Finishing the brand guide will take me 5 more days, and I am still working on it. If you would prefer, I could put that work on hold and begin the landing page first. Would that ordering be better?

For the landing page, I submitted an hourly proposal at $140. Does that rate work for you?

speaker: client
text:
Hi Marissa,

I was attending my grandson's eighth-grade promotion at Harbor Ridge Academy. yesterday, so apologies for not replying then.

Before the brand guide is finalized, I suggest briefly testing how the current styles translate to the SaaS UI and, to a lesser extent, the website. That exploration should help move development forward while potentially revealing design decisions that can feed into the final guide.

For the next "landing page plus" job, an hourly arrangement feels too open-ended while I am operating in bootstrapped mode, even though I would like us to build an ongoing design partnership. Could we instead try a fixed price of $1,800 for this engagement and see how it works?

To indicate the standard I am aiming for without preempting our discussions or UI design choices, I have attached a Google Workspace UI example. I would like the resulting UI design quality to equal or exceed it.

If this proposal sounds acceptable, let me know and I will hire you for the next job. Assuming you accept, an early review meeting would be useful; we could return to the office or meet by video.

Best,
Derek

speaker: freelancer
text:
What a special occasion—congratulations to your grandson on completing eighth grade!

The examples make me think the proposed project may cover both the website landing page and the web-app UI/UX. Could we separate the pricing, using $900 for the landing page and my hourly rate for the web app? Until I understand what the web-app scope involves, I would be hesitant to lock both areas into one fixed price.

speaker: freelancer
text: Another kick-off meeting sounds good; I'm happy to use it to get the work started!
